---
name: orchestrate-plan
description: "Run PLAN.md in one session — you verify and re-plan, a cheaper subagent executes each step"
---
Execute `PLAN.md` as its coordinator. You are the strong reasoning model: you verify every result and do all re-planning. A cheaper, faster subagent makes every edit.

Extra instructions (may be empty): the request given after the command name

Delegate execution to:

- Claude Code: the `plan-executor` subagent.
- Copilot CLI: the `plan-executor` custom agent (or the general-purpose subagent, with its model set through `/subagents`).
- VS Code: the Implementer agent for your setup.

Check that Git runs the repository's hooks in the clone you work in, so `.githooks/commit-msg` strips AI agent attribution from every commit before it can reach a pull request: run `git config core.hooksPath`. When it names a folder called `.githooks`, they run. When it prints nothing, the repository has a `.githooks` folder and no `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and the folder `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` prints holds no hook of its own (a file whose name doesn't end in `.sample`), run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Otherwise never change it: say in your reply that `.githooks/commit-msg` doesn't run in this clone, and that `.template/Update-Project.ps1` prints how to run it alongside the clone's own hooks.

For each step whose heading starts with `### [ ]`, in order:

1. Delegate the step with a self-contained task. The subagent does not see this conversation, so include the step number, the full step text copied from `PLAN.md`, the Context for the executor section, and the instruction to escalate with `[?]` instead of improvising.
2. When it returns, run the step's Done-when command yourself from the repository root, also when the subagent reports that it could not run it: a check the subagent made instead does not count. When the Context for the executor has a `- Prelude:` line, run its command, `<prelude>`, first in the same PowerShell: `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0; try { . <prelude> } catch { $_; "prelude failed"; exit 2 }; if (-not $? -or $LASTEXITCODE) { "prelude failed"; exit 2 }; <the Done-when command>`. When it exits 2 and the output's last line, apart from any exit code your shell adds, is `prelude failed`, the check never ran: stop, show me the prelude's error, and say to fix the `- prelude:` line in the `## Landing` section of `AGENTS.md`, or the script it names, and the plan's `- Prelude:` line.
3. Passed: mark the step `[x]` if the subagent did not. Run `git status`: a changed file the step does not list is a deviation to resolve before you commit. Then stage only the files the step lists, with `git add <those files>` — never `git add -A` or `git add .`, and never `PLAN.md`, which stays untracked and is never committed or pushed — run `git commit -m "Plan step N: <title>"`, and continue with the next step.
4. Escalated (`[?]`) or failed: re-plan the step yourself — diagnose it, rewrite or split it, record any decision under Decisions, remove the Escalation line, reset it to `[ ]` — then run `git commit --allow-empty -m "Re-plan step N: <title>"` (the plan is untracked, so this commit only records the re-plan), and delegate the step again. When `PLAN.md` has an `Issue:` line and the re-plan changed the Decisions or added or removed steps, post a two-to-five-line comment on each issue on that line saying what changed and why — `gh issue comment <number> --body-file <file>`, or `glab issue note <number> --message <text>` on GitLab — yourself, never through the subagent. A session's own tooling can add agent attribution to what it posts, on GitHub or GitLab, whichever AI agent, assistant or model runs the session: a Claude Code cloud session appends a line `---` and then a footer line `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/…)_` to each pull request description, issue, comment and review-thread reply it creates, through `gh` and the GitHub MCP tools alike, and other agents, such as Copilot's coding agent, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Jules or GitLab Duo, can append a line of their own that says the text was generated, written or created with or by an AI tool, or a link to the agent's session or task, while `gh` or `glab` in a local session appends nothing. So straight after each command that creates or edits a pull request or merge request description, an issue, or a top-level comment or note, read back what was saved, from the repository it went to. On GitHub: `gh pr view <number> --json body --jq .body` for a pull request, `gh issue view <number> --json body --jq .body` for an issue, each with the `--repo <owner/repo>` the command that posted had, when it had one, or `gh api "repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/comments/<id>" --jq .body` for a comment, where `<owner>/<repo>` is the part of the URL the command printed between `github.com/` and `/issues/` or `/pull/`, and `<id>` is the number after `#issuecomment-` in it. On GitLab: the `description` in what `glab mr view <number> --output json` prints for a merge request or `glab issue view <number> --output json` prints for an issue, each with the `--repo <group/project>` the command that posted had, when it had one, or the `body` in what `glab api "projects/:id/merge_requests/<number>/notes/<id>"` prints for a note, with `issues` in place of `merge_requests` for a note on an issue and, for a note in another project, that project's URL-encoded path, such as `group%2Fproject`, in place of `:id`, where `<id>` is the number after `#note_` in the URL the command printed, or the `id` the API returned. When the last lines of it that aren't blank are agent attribution, each a line that starts, after any symbols or underscores, with words such as `Generated with`, `Generated by`, `Created by` or `Made with` and then an AI tool, agent or model, such as `[Claude Code`, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Gemini, Grok or GitLab Duo, or a line that holds only a link to an agent's session or task, such as a `claude.ai/code/session_`, `chatgpt.com/codex/tasks/`, `cursor.com/agents/`, `app.devin.ai/sessions/` or `jules.google.com/task/` link, remove those lines, the `---` line above them, when there is one, and the blank lines between and after them, and keep every other line as it was. Remove it in that same repository, through a route that doesn't append it again. On GitHub, use the GitHub MCP tools when the session has them, because in a Claude Code cloud session an edit through `gh` appends the footer again: `update_pull_request` with the new body for a pull request, `issue_write` with `method: update` and the new body for an issue, or `update_issue_comment` with the comment's id and the new body for a comment; without them, write the new body to a file and run `gh pr edit <number> --body-file <file>`, `gh issue edit <number> --body-file <file>` or `gh api -X PATCH "repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/comments/<id>" -F body=@<file>`, with the same `--repo`. On GitLab, write the new text to a file and run `glab mr update <number> --description (Get-Content -Raw <file>)`, `glab issue update <number> --description (Get-Content -Raw <file>)` or `glab api --method PUT "projects/:id/merge_requests/<number>/notes/<id>" -F body=@<file>`, with the same `--repo`, project and `issues` as the read-back. Then read it back once more; when the attribution is still there, the route appended it again: on GitHub, try the other route once, `gh` after the GitHub MCP tools or the GitHub MCP tools after `gh`, and when it is still there, or there is no other route, as on GitLab, leave it and list it in your report, and for a pull request or merge request description also say that the `Commit attribution` check may fail until a person deletes those lines. Two posts are exceptions. Never edit a `/review` comment, even when it came back with attribution: the `/review` request reads it back itself and deletes it when anything was appended, because NCode Review acts only on the comment as it was created, so an edited `/review` comment requests no review. A reply on a review thread is the other exception: on GitHub nothing a Claude Code cloud session can call edits one without its footer, so post each reply as these instructions say anyway, because every finding still gets its reply, and list the replies in your report as ones that may carry the footer; on GitLab, a reply on a discussion is a note, read back and edited as above with `discussions/<discussion id>/notes/<id>` in place of `notes/<id>`.
5. Stop and ask me when a step has been re-planned twice and still does not pass, or when re-planning would change the Goal or Out of scope.

Make code changes yourself only as a last resort, after a step has been re-planned twice, and say so in the summary. Finish with a table of step, result, delegations, re-plans and notes, then give the next command: `/review-plan-diff`, or `/review-plan-diff <worktree name>` from another session.
